lens: Performance — allocation on hot paths, zero-copy preservation, blocking I/O at scale, benchmark coverage, perf-budget regression gates
answer: The four new pub fn sub-checks (check_rust_default_language, check_naming_convention, check_scorecard_render, check_consensus_debate_evidence) all execute blocking filesystem I/O — std::fs::read_dir and std::fs::read_to_string — without any benchmark, no async/parallel dispatch, and with eager format!() string allocation for every finding, including unconditional findings that are always emitted regardless of result. At today's file counts (1 multispectrum file, 8 per-change files) the cost is immaterial, but the code shape scales as O(N) blocking syscalls per sub-check invocation with no upper-bound cap on either I/O or allocation. Two sub-checks (check_scorecard_render, check_consensus_debate_evidence) read full file contents into heap-allocated Strings via read_to_string just to call str::contains twice; a stat-only or header-read approach would eliminate the copy entirely. check_naming_convention allocates a String per directory entry unconditionally via to_string_lossy().to_string() even for entries that are immediately skipped. No benchmark exists; all four functions are cold-path today but would become warm-path if the lane runs in a pre-push hook or CI inner loop at 10x file volume (80+ per-change files). There is no perf-budget regression test that would catch a future degradation.
key_claims: check_scorecard_render and check_consensus_debate_evidence call std::fs::read_to_string on every .json file in two directories; at 10x file volume (80 per-change files) this is 80+ blocking heap-allocating reads per invocation with no async dispatch.

check_naming_convention calls to_string_lossy().to_string() on every directory entry unconditionally — this allocates an owned String even for dotfiles that are immediately skipped via the starts_with('.') guard.

All four functions use format!() to construct finding strings eagerly, including strings that are always emitted (e.g., the 'NOT YET ARMED' lines) regardless of whether any violation was found — these could be &'static str literals at zero cost.
No benchmark (criterion or otherwise) exists for any of the four sub-checks; the perf claim is implicit ('it's a check crate, it runs once') without evidence.
No regression baseline exists; a future O(N^2) regression (e.g., nested read_dir) would pass CI silently.
check_scorecard_render reads full file bytes to call contains() on two fixed key strings; a BufReader line-scan or mmap-based search would preserve zero-copy semantics that the current code abandons.
uncertainty_areas: Invocation frequency is unknown: if these sub-checks run only once per release pipeline (truly cold), the blocking I/O concern is negligible in practice; if they run in a pre-push hook or watch mode the concern becomes material.

Whether the evidence/multispectrum and evidence/per-change directories are bounded by convention (small) or unbounded (grows with every change) is not documented; the perf class assignment depends on this.
Rust's default stack-based I/O buffering and OS page cache may absorb the read_to_string cost on re-invocations within the same process; this is not measured.

detailed_findings.finding: std::fs::read_dir on scripts/ — stat-only, no file reads. Acceptable. Two format!() strings always allocated unconditionally; both could be &'static str. Minor.

to_string_lossy().to_string() at lib.rs:783 allocates an owned String for every directory entry including those immediately skipped by starts_with('.'). Should be: let s = name.to_string_lossy(); (Cow<str>, no alloc on valid UTF-8). Violations Vec capped at 10 — correct. format!() strings in findings allocated unconditionally.
detailed_findings.severity: moderate — allocation per entry including skipped entries

detailed_findings.finding: std::fs::read_to_string at lib.rs:842 loads every .json file fully into a heap String to call .contains() twice. At 10x volume (80 files) this is 80 full-file heap allocations. A BufReader line-scan exiting early on first match of both keys would avoid full-file reads. Zero-copy path (mmap or read-with-limit) entirely absent.
detailed_findings.severity: high — copy introduced where streaming/early-exit was feasible; scales O(N * avg_file_size)

detailed_findings.finding: Same pattern as check_scorecard_render: read_to_string at lib.rs:883 for every .json file in two dirs to call .contains() for two string variants of 'meta_review_triggered'. Same O(N * file_size) allocation concern. Additionally, the debate_dir scan at lib.rs:894 allocates a String via to_string_lossy() for every entry just to call ends_with(); could use OsStr::to_str() with a borrow.
detailed_findings.severity: high — copy introduced where zero-copy or early-exit was feasible

perf_budget_recommendation: Add a criterion benchmark group 'sub-check-suite' covering all four functions against a fixture workspace with 100 per-change files and 10 multispectrum files. Gate CI on < 200ms wall-time for the full suite. Replace read_to_string+contains with BufReader line-scan with early exit in check_scorecard_render and check_consensus_debate_evidence. Replace to_string_lossy().to_string() with to_string_lossy() (Cow) where the String is only used for comparison or starts_with.
